_comment: TASK-470 (Theme F) committed regression thresholds — the single source of truth A1/A2/A3/B/C are judged against. TRANSPORT baselines are TASK-455's captured LocalAgreement-2 numbers (stt-loss-report.json: commit-latency P50 6023.2 / P99 7624.2 ms, partial_revision.rate 0.0, seq.gap_count 0, audio_coverage_ratio 0.996). QUALITY baselines are null until the orchestrator's LIVE-STACK scorecard run captures them on the clinical fixtures; an ABSOLUTE bootstrap ceiling/floor gates them in the meantime. Tighten quality 'baseline' to the captured value (keeping the documented epsilon) once the live scorecard lands.

medical_wer._note: Lower is better; GUARDRAIL. ceiling 0.35 is a conservative bootstrap for clean scripted clinical reads on whisper-large-v3-turbo (SOTA short-form English medical WER is ~0.10-0.20; 0.35 leaves headroom yet still catches a badly-regressed model). epsilon 0.05 = the allowed drift once baseline is captured.

keyterm_recall._note: Higher is better; GUARDRAIL — the 'did we drop the drug/dose/finding' catcher. floor 0.70 bootstrap; epsilon 0.05 drift once baseline captured.

keyphrase_recall._note: Higher is better; GUARDRAIL. Subsequence (looser) recall for longer descriptive phrases. floor 0.70 bootstrap.

partial_revision_rate._note: Lower is better; the A1 guardrail (a tentative tail must NOT increase caption churn). TASK-455 baseline 0.0 on the …402 pipeline; epsilon 0.02 tolerates float/sampling noise while still catching real flicker.

commit_latency_ms._note: Lower is better; GUARDRAIL for A1 (conservative commit must not regress), TARGET for A2. Inference-dominated on the offline whisper-turbo host, so the gate is on the RATIO delta (15%), not the absolute — transport must not add >15% over TASK-455's baseline.

seq_gap_count._note: Dropped captions; GUARDRAIL — zero tolerance. TASK-455 baseline gap_count 0 on the connected path.

audio_coverage_ratio._note: Higher is better; GUARDRAIL. TASK-455 baseline 0.996 (max final endTime / audio seconds). epsilon 0.005 absorbs VAD-tail jitter.
